analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (a date bump and a new paragraph near head lines 1577-1588) and a comment block in docs/threat-model.yaml (head lines 41-48). The reviewed head excerpts of cli-reference.md (lines 2475-3086) are unchanged context, and I found no executable or configuration change in them. The new text says that cluster waits, the 10-minute pair-start wait and the desktop earnings windows compare Dates with timeIntervalSince(_:). It says SDK 27.2 back-deploys the Date >= and <= operators as weak imports that pre-release macOS 27.2 lacks, which crashed the provider in a loop. It says thresholds and results are unchanged, and that scripts/check-date-comparisons.py and scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py (the latter in release builds) refuse the pattern. The threat-model comment records the same for the App Attest key-generation budget, enrollment resume, stall restart and key history, framed as A-018 availability. It explicitly does not revalidate older threat entries.

Security reading: no change to authorization, attestation, encryption, App Attest serving authorization (A-016, TB-011) or the cache threat T-041. The described change is an availability hardening. It claims behavior-preserving thresholds, but I could not check the source or scripts, so that claim and the existence and efficacy of the two scripts are unverified. Next passes should confirm that the swapped comparisons in the App Attest expiry, freshness and grant-lifetime paths preserve the boundary semantics. For example, replacing `>=` with timeIntervalSince could change equality handling by one tick and so shift the expiry edge. They should also confirm that the release weak-import check actually fails the build. The doc links (../developer/build.md#sdk-27-release-builds-and-caches) point to files outside this batch. No findings.
